 Cooper Flagg put on a show with 33 points (13-of-19 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), nine rebounds, six assists, two steals, and a block in Mavericks win over the Rockets. 
 The Mavericks beat the undefeated Houston Rockets in this game and Flagg made the big time bucket to lead them to a win. He’s already one of the best players in fantasy basketball and there’s no sign of this slowing down. Getting him at the backend of the first round in many redraft leagues has turned into a massive steal at his ADP. Sit back and enjoy the ride if you have him.

 Cooper Flagg had 26 points (10-of-23 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s 120-96 victory over the Thunder. 
 Flagg is averaging 25.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks through four games this year. The 19-year-old’s game Wednesday against the Thunder was even more impressive considering he also had zero turnovers. Easily the best young player in the league, Flagg may already have elevated himself into being part of the MVP conversation. 
 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) returned to the lineup on Monday and finished with 29 points (12-of-23 FGs), six rebounds, 11 assists, four steals, two blocks, two three-pointers and five turnovers in a 113-109 win over the Heat. 
 The initial expectation was that this would be a multi-game absence for Flagg. However, it only ended up being one game on the sidelines for him, and he returned in a big way in this game. The only knock on Flagg so far this season has been the high turnover numbers, but he has been truly fantastic in every other category. Of course, the sample size is small, but if he continues to produce at this level, he will have absolutely been worth taking in the first round of fantasy drafts.

He left Friday’s game against the Pacers with a shoulder injury and subsequently missed Saturday’s game against the Spurs.  Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Flagg being listed as questionable on the Mavericks’ initial injury report is good news for fantasy managers. After he sustained a shoulder injury during Friday’s win over the Pacers, expectations were that the reigning Rookie of the Year would miss a few days. Now, Flagg could miss just one game after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. If he returns, Zaccharie Risacher will head to the bench. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall produced 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of- 3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 With Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg unavailable, Marshall moved into the starting lineup for Saturday’s game. He took on playmaking responsibilities for large stretches of the 122-106 defeat, dishing out five of the 12 assists recorded by Mavericks starters. While Irving should be back for Monday’s game against the Heat, Flagg’s shoulder injury may keep him out for multiple games. If so, Marshall is worth streaming in deep leagues.

 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is out for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 No surprise here as Flagg left Friday night’s game against the Pacers with shoulder soreness. Expect the Mavericks to play through Kyrie Irving in his absence against the Spurs on Saturday. 
 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Cooper Flagg was on his way with 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, three steals, a block, and two 3-pointers before exiting with shoulder injury. 
 Cooper Flagg is ascending and it is happening quickly. He entered first round conversations in redraft leagues this season and is an easy top 8 asset in dynasty leagues. While he’s like Jayson Tatum in terms of a fantasy player, he will be one of the main faces of the league moving forward. Now, we await the severity of the shoulder injury he sustained. It’s officially listed as soreness, but we’ll get more details tomorrow or the day after.

 Pascal Siakam shot 5-of-17 from the field and 3-of-5 from the foul line in Friday’s loss to the Heat, scoring 13 points with five rebounds, four assists and two steals.
 After a stellar showing on Wednesday in Indiana’s first game since losing Tyrese Haliburton to a hamstring strain, Siakam was held in check by the Timberwolves. He missed all five three-point attempts, which hurt his overall field-goal percentage. Haliburton doesn’t have a firm return timeline, but the Pacers will rely even more on Siakam in their point guard’s absence. Nights like Friday won’t become the norm for Siakam, but no Haliburton is a big deal.

 Dillon Brooks had 22 points (9-of-12 FGs), a rebound, two assists, a steal, and four 3-pointers in 20 minutes before getting ejected on Friday.
 Dillon Brooks was hitting his shots and was a big reason they stayed in this game. He kicked out his leg on a jump shot which was viewed as excessive and resulted in a flagrant 2 foul and an ejection. Obviously the ejection isn’t great but it is part of the deal with Brooks. Even with it, he still put up a lot of points and could’ve had an even better line. His next opportunity to play will be on Monday against the Warriors.

 Quenton Jackson amassed 24 points (9-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Heat.
 One game doesn’t make a role player a must-roster in fantasy basketball, especially if injuries have expanded their role. For Jackson, Obi Toppin’s absence on Friday meant more shots for the healthy Pacers reserves, even if they don’t play the same position. The 24 points were one shy of his career-high, and Jackson’s final line lacked only a blocked shot. The Pacers end their week with a game against the Nets on Sunday.

 Andrew Nembhard finished Friday’s loss to the Heat with 22 points (8-of-16 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists and five three-pointers.
 After shooting 5-of-16 from the field in Wednesday’s loss to the 76ers, Nembhard was more efficient on Friday. In addition to shooting 50 percent from the field, he finished one assist shy of a double-double. With Tyrese Haliburton and T.J. McConnell sidelined, Nembhard will have to do more as both a scorer and playmaker. In theory, that should raise his short-term fantasy ceiling.

 Klay Thompson accumulated 25 points (9-of-14 FGs), three assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pacers.
 Entering Friday, Thompson was shooting 31.7 percent from the field and 32.1 percent from three. To say a night like Friday was needed would be an understatement. Against the Pacers, Thompson shot 7-of-12 from beyond the arc, and 25 points is the most he has scored in a game since January 15, as a member of the Mavericks. With neither Giannis Antetokounmpo nor Bam Adebayo offering much perimeter shooting as Miami’s top two offensive options, Thompson needs to hit shots consistently. Friday’s 145-point outburst showed what can happen when he and the other Heat shooters are productive.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Bam Adebayo recorded 27 points (11-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals in Friday’s win over the Pacers.
 After scoring 24 points in Wednesday’s win over the Hawks, Adebayo was even more productive against the Pacers. He shot 11-of-12 inside the arc, including 10-of-11 in the paint. Add in the rebounds and steals, and Bam had a good night. There’s still plenty of basketball to be played, but Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo appeared to have improved chemistry in Miami’s last two games.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo finished Friday’s win over the Pacers with 31 points (13-of-18 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), 17 rebounds, 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer.
 The Pacers had no answer for Giannis on Friday, as he scored 24 of his 31 points in the paint. The partnership between Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo looked a bit awkward at the start of the season, which isn’t surprising. But both have looked more comfortable in the last two games, both Heat victories. And it helps that the Heat shot 18-of-40 from three against the Pacers, which provided much-needed spacing on offense.

 Isaiah Jackson finished Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and four blocks.
 Friday was a good night for managers rostering Jackson. In addition to matching his season-high in steals, the Clippers’ starting center blocked four shots. In the first four games of the season, Jackson blocked only two shots. Jackson’s defensive potential and field-goal percentage can make him valuable to fantasy managers, even though he’s sharing center responsibilities with Brook Lopez (15 points, six rebounds and one block). Against the Timberwolves, both played 21 minutes.

 Rui Hachimura accounted for 12 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Back in the Clippers’ lineup after missing Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, Hachimura played 26 minutes against the Timberwolves. He didn’t shoot well, but Rui recorded a few steals in his return. Kobe Sanders, who started on Wednesday, finished with seven points, four rebounds and two steals in 24 minutes off the bench. The Clippers play one more game this week, Sunday night against the Warriors.

 Darius Garland amassed 24 points (10-of-22 FGs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Counting Friday, Garland has recorded at least five turnovers in four consecutive games. He recorded five against the Timberwolves, a negative mark on an otherwise decent night individually. Because of injuries to Brandon Ingram, Bradley Beal and Max Strus, Garland has had to shoulder a heavier offensive workload, and that hasn’t done his nine-cat value any favors.
